title: Selection assay to identify desiccation tolerant bacteria.
author: Dalia Molina-Romero

steps_raw.instruction: 1 Selection assay to identify desiccation tolerant bacteria. Dalia Molina-Romero1,2¶, Antonino Baez1, Miguel Castañeda-Lucio3, Luis Ernesto Fuentes-Ramírez1, María del Rocío Bustillos-Cristales1, Osvaldo Rodríguez-Andrade1, Yolanda Elizabeth Morales-García1,2, Antonio Munive1, Verónica Quintero-Hernández4 and Jesús Muñoz-Rojas*1. 1Laboratorio de Ecología Molecular Microbiana (LEMM), Centro de Investigaciones en Ciencias Microbiológicas (CICM), Instituto de Ciencias (IC), Benemérita Universidad Autónoma de Puebla (BUAP). 2Laboratorio de Biología Molecular y Mi crobiología, Facultad de Ciencias Biológicas , BUAP. 3Genética Molecular Microbiana, CICM, IC-BUAP. 4CONACYT, LEMM, CICM, IC-BUAP. ¶First Author *Corresponding author E-mail: joymerre@yahoo.com.mx (JMR) Abstract We describe a method to evaluate bacterial tolerance to air desiccation at 30 °C and 50% relative humidity. Growth medium SYP broth is used for the cultivation of different bacteria until stationary phase. The composition of this medium is sucrose 10g, yeast extract 1g, K2HPO4 1g and KH2PO4 3g, a final pH of 6.2[1,2]. Description of the method Bacteria are grown until stationary phase in SYP liquid medium , because at this growth stage cells are able to resist stresses better than cells i n exponential phase [3]. Afterward, bacterial cells are harvested by centrifugation, washed twice with sterile water, and resuspended in the initial volume (45 ml) of sterile water. Before desiccation, the number of cultivable cells is quantified by quintuplicate using the massive stamping drop plate (MSDP) in SYP medium plates [4]. For each strain, thirty sterile polypropylene tubes are filled with 500 µL of the bacterial suspension and covered with a sterile cotton cap. T he tubes with the bacterial suspension are placed in a desiccation chamber at 30 °C and 55 % relative humidity (RH). Under those conditions w ater of each tube is completely loosed

2 after six days and this is corroborated by the constant weight of the tubes (an example is showed in Figure 1). We recommend the counting of cultivable cells, after rehydration of desiccated cells, every three days for a period of twelve days using the MSDP method. For the samples of 3 days after the beginning of desiccation (DABD) the tubes are filled with water to the initial 500 µL. For completel y desiccated sam ples (6, 9, and 12 DABD), 500 µL of water must be added to each tube and after 40 minutes with occasional shaking, cell re-hydratation must be completed. The bacterial survival ratio (BSR) is reported as the ratio of the log number of bacterial cells present in the suspension at any time after the beginning of desiccation (AbD) plus one to the log number of viable cells before desiccation (BD), multiplied by 100, i.e., BSR=(log AbD+1/log BD) x 100 [3]. The BSR is a parameter that allowed us to quantify the desiccation tolerance of bacteria. Figure 1. Water loss in Sphingomonas sp. OF178 samples subjected to desiccation at 30 °C and 50% HR.
